stem.en: In many animal cells, division stops when cells touch their neighbours. What happens when cells lose this control?

text.en: They stop dividing entirely, and the tissue cannot repair itself.

feedback.en: This is the opposite of what happens.

text.en: They form daughter cells that are too small to survive.

feedback.en: The change is in how many cells form, not in how small they are.

text.en: They keep dividing, and this can form a tumour.

feedback.en: Yes. Division carries on when it should stop.

text.en: They divide more slowly than the body needs.

feedback.en: Losing a control on division does not slow it down.

explanation.en: Contact inhibition normally stops division. Cancer cells lose this control and keep dividing uncontrollably, and this leads to the formation of tumours.

hints.en: What does contact inhibition normally do to division?
